newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 48-hr peso closes sharply stronger.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 48-hr peso closes sharply stronger.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended earlier strength to close firmer across the board on Monday due to some foreign investors stepping back into Mexico and local dealers selling long dollar positions, traders said.

"Some (local) banks had taken long dollar positions, thinking that the peso would be trading at more than 8.10 per dollar by now...but they had to dump them as they were missing out on high money market rates in pesos," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 5.5 centavos firmer, at 7.8930/7.8980 and 7.8900/7.8950 per dollar.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 3.3 centavos firmer at 7.9100/7.9170 per dollar.
Traders said the tentative return of U.S. investors to Mexico could be due to what they foresaw as a favorable result for the Mexican financial markets in the U.S. presidential race on Tuesday.
Dealers added that the peso could return to levels of 7.85 per dollar in the event that primary Cetes rates fell only marginally at Tuesday's auction.
